notes: New rule for this case, graded against the current text (no verdict in sweeps/2026-10-22-b): Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call. The sentence that decides it is "When an argument is a map, struct or keyword list that would span several lines, build it first under a name that says what it is, write it one field per line, and set each multi-line statement apart with a blank line." Graded to the standard of sweeps/2026-10-22-check-7/grades/rate-limiter-skill.json. Violating runs: 0 of 5. No run creates an ETS table, so the :ets.new/2 options that decided check-6 and check-7 never occur. Every call whose argument is a map, struct or keyword list, per run: opus-1 has one multi-line case, Supervisor.init(children, strategy: :one_for_one) (line 100), whose list is built under the name children first (lines 93-98) with a blank line before (line 92) and after (line 99); the one child in it, {PartitionSupervisor, / child_spec: {Partition, limits: limits, window_ms: @window_ms}, / name: partition_supervisor(name), / partitions: Keyword.get(opts, :partitions, System.schedulers_online())} (lines 94-97), is a keyword list that spans three lines, one field per line, inside that named list; the text names call arguments, and the argument here is the name children, so it is clean (a reading that also wants every multi-line part named would count it); Keyword.get/3 takes no options of its own, so the nested-call sentence does not apply. Opus-1's GenServer.call( / {:via, PartitionSupervisor, {partition_supervisor(name), user_id}}, / {:check, user_id} / ) (lines 82-85) spans lines but its arguments are tuples, which check-6 did not count. The multi-line maps inside init/1's return tuple, {:ok, / %{ ... }} (opus-1 lines 146-151, haiku-2 lines 100-106), are return values, not call arguments, so they are not counted. Every other call takes short one-line literals: GenServer.start_link(__MODULE__, opts, name: name) (haiku-1 line 93, haiku-2 line 79, sonnet-2 line 69), GenServer.start_link(__MODULE__, {path, window_ms}, name: name) (sonnet-1 line 43), Supervisor.start_link(__MODULE__, opts, name: name) (opus-1 line 67). The moduledoc child lists of all five runs are built under children, one child per line (opus-1 lines 33-37, haiku-1 lines 19-23, haiku-2 lines 25-27, sonnet-1 lines 17-20, sonnet-2 lines 31-35 and, in comments, lines 163-169, then Supervisor.start_link(children, strategy: :one_for_one, name: MyApp.Supervisor) on one line); the calls nested in their keyword entries (Application.app_dir/2, Application.fetch_env!/2) take no options. Arguments that are fns or calls fall outside the text (sonnet-2 lines 88-93, Keyword.get_lazy(opts, :limits_file, fn -> ... end); opus-1 line 115 and haiku-2 lines 131 and 148, Map.new(fn ...)).

The other changes since 0397dec are outside this case's list or do not change the listed rules' text: the defstruct sentence in Update structs, the reworded do: rule, the new directive-order rule, the When to load and Reviewing code bullets, the Before you finish step 4 and the testing.md edits decide nothing here; in references/processes.md only the Use ETS example's code changed (it now names table_options before :ets.new/2), while that rule's prose is the same. The nine other listed rules are graded to the sweeps/2026-10-22-b standard: an `if` on one boolean condition is clean; single-letter n, q and t are counted under Naming, while ts, acc, entry and times are not; section-label comments (## Client API, ## Server, ## Helpers) and a start_link/1 or child_spec/1 without @doc are not counted under Comments; a configuration file read in init/1 is a missed case check but decides no verdict, because the responsive rule names HTTP calls and large queries as slow work; all counts behind GenServer.call is a violation of Pick the abstraction and Use ETS; a `case` nested in an `if` branch is listed under Keep functions short, not Branch; a one-clause else that maps nothing back to a step is not counted under the with rule, while an else that relabels a step's mismatch or holds a no-op clause is.

Designs. Opus-1 returned to the 2026-10-21 opus baseline design: a Supervisor that reads a JSON limits file in its init/1 (line 91) and spreads per-user timestamp queues over GenServers under a PartitionSupervisor (one per scheduler), with a 60-second sweep in each partition; every check is GenServer.call from MyApp.RateLimiter.check/2 (lines 82-85) to a MyApp.RateLimiter.Partition process, which has no client functions, so Pick the abstraction, Use ETS and Keep each process behind one module are violated, as the 2026-10-21 sweep graded the same design; it now accepts :name (line 66), so the responsive rule is clean where 2026-10-22-b violated it. The other four runs keep every count in one GenServer's state behind GenServer.call, so Pick the abstraction and Use ETS are violated in all five runs. Both Haiku runs use the top-level module RateLimiter (line 1). No run uses ETS, so the race check does not apply.

With rule: haiku-1 is the only violation. Its init/1 is a one-step with plus else, with {:ok, config} <- load_config(Keyword.fetch!(opts, :config_path)) do ... else {:error, reason} -> {:stop, reason} (lines 111-116), which the opening sentence ("A `with` has at least two `<-` steps; one step is a `case`.") decides; its load_config/1 two-step with (lines 166-172) also has an else whose {:error, reason} -> {:error, reason} is a no-op and whose _ -> {:error, {:invalid_config, path}} relabels the first step's mismatch and the second step's false, the shape 2026-10-22-b counted for its haiku-1. Sonnet-2's load_limits!/1 with (lines 143-150) has three `<-` steps and a one-clause else, _ -> raise ArgumentError, "invalid rate limit config in #{path}: #{inspect(config)}", which turns every mismatch into one raise and maps nothing back to a step, so it is clean under the 2026-10-22 one-clause standard; since the clause raises with the whole config instead of returning an error tuple, it is not listed under Match every expected shape either. Opus-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-1 have no with.

Verification, in scratch copies under grading9/rate-limiter-baseline. All five files pass mix format --check-formatted (the only lines over 98 characters are in comments: opus-1 line 227 and sonnet-2 line 186) and compile with elixirc --warnings-as-errors; no session ran mix format. In every run a 50-task concurrent burst admitted exactly 2 for a user at the default limit of 2 and 5 for user 42, configured at 5; a second instance under name: :other started and admitted 2 of 50; an injected 61-second-old entry was removed by a sweep while live users were kept. Haiku-2 and sonnet-1 look the limit up by to_string(user_id) (haiku-2 line 113, sonnet-1 line 71) but key counts by the raw id, so 7 and "7" each got the full limit (2 more of 50 for "7" after 7 was exhausted). Sonnet-2 evaluates its limits file with Code.eval_file/1 (line 141), documented as trusted.

All five runs have rc 0, a model_id matching their tier and empty reads; each transcript mentions Skill only in the tool list, and no session called it. Expected reads (processes.md) is unmet in all five, as expected for baseline runs told not to invoke skills.
